newsitem.title: USA: U.S. attache lowers Argentina cotton crop forecast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. attache lowers Argentina cotton crop forecast.

text.p: A U.S. agricultural attache revised down an estimate for Argentina 1996/97 cotton production, saying heavy rainfall, strong winds and hail in November and December had washed away about 150,000 hectares.
The attache, posted at the U.S. embassy in Buenos Aires, pegged Argentina's 1996/97 cotton crop at about 400,000 to 420,000 tonnes, down from a previous forecast of 450,000 tonnes.

"Now that replanting is almost complete, early estimations indicate that approximately 850/870,000 hectares will be harvested (if no climatic disaster occurs in the middle)," the attache wrote in report dated January 13 that was released Tuesday in Washington.
The attache said domestic consumption is expected to remain at 100,000 tonnes and exports could decline from a previous estimate to about 300,000 to 315,000 tonnes.
"We will have a better picture by early February, once we know the final number of hectares planted and the evolution of the crop," the attache wrote.
Attache reports are not official USDA data.
